name: South Africa
legalSystem: mixed (Roman-Dutch civil law and common law)
note: A doctor certifies a natural death, and anyone present or in charge of the burial gives notice to Home Affairs with that certificate. Home Affairs completes the death register and issues the burial order. Including the particulars in the National Population Register is itself the registration, so the death is recorded centrally at once. State departments, banks and insurers may be given register information on prescribed terms. Unnatural deaths go to the police and the magistrate under the Inquests Act.

steps.title: Doctor examines the body and is satisfied death was natural
steps.who: A medical practitioner who did not attend the deceased but examined the corpse after death.
steps.summary: A doctor who examines the body after death and is satisfied it was natural may issue the prescribed certificate.

steps.title: Attending doctor certifies the cause of a natural death
steps.localName: medical certificate of cause of death (DHA-1663)
steps.who: The medical practitioner who attended the deceased before death.
steps.trigger: A death the practitioner is satisfied was due to natural causes.
steps.summary: The attending practitioner must issue the prescribed certificate stating the cause of death. That certificate is the vehicle for the notice of death.

steps.title: Doctor refers an unnatural death to the police
steps.trigger: Opinion that the death was due to other than natural causes.
steps.summary: The doctor must not certify and must tell a police officer, who acts under section 3 of the Inquests Act.

steps.title: Anyone reports a suspected unnatural death to the police
steps.who: Any person who has reason to believe a person died other than from natural causes.
steps.trigger: Reason to believe the death was not natural.
steps.summary: Report to a police officer as soon as possible; failure is an offence (fine up to R1 000).

steps.title: Police investigate and report to the magistrate
steps.who: Any police officer; the magistrate of the district (inquest).
steps.trigger: Reason to believe a death was from other than natural causes.
steps.summary: Police investigate the circumstances and report the death to the magistrate; the body is examined by a district surgeon or other doctor.

steps.title: Give notice of the death to Home Affairs
steps.who: Any person who was present at the death, became aware of it, or has charge of the burial (typically the family or undertaker).
steps.trigger: The death, with the medical certificate.
steps.summary: Notice is given as soon as practicable, by means of the medical certificate, to a person authorised by the Director-General of Home Affairs. Failing to give a required notice is an offence (up to five years).

steps.title: Home Affairs completes the death register and issues the burial order
steps.who: An officer authorised by the Director-General (Home Affairs office, or authorised police officer or undertaker).
steps.trigger: Satisfaction from the certificate that the death was natural.
steps.summary: The authorised person completes the death register and issues the burial order; no burial may take place without it, and the person in charge of the burial hands it to the cemetery.

steps.title: Registrar refers a doubtful death to the police
steps.trigger: Reasonable doubt whether the death was natural.
steps.summary: No burial order is issued and the police are informed; an order already issued is withdrawn if the body is not yet buried.

steps.title: Police register an unnatural death after the post-mortem
steps.who: The police officer concerned (or an authorised officer), on the doctor's certificate that the body is no longer needed.
steps.summary: The death register is completed without stating a cause and a burial order issued.

steps.title: The death is entered in the National Population Register
steps.summary: Particulars from the notice are included in the population register, and that inclusion is itself the registration of the death.

steps.title: Home Affairs issues the death certificate
steps.who: The Director-General of Home Affairs, on application.
steps.summary: After registration the Director-General issues the prescribed death certificate, which is prima facie evidence in court.

steps.title: Hand in the deceased's identity card for cancellation
steps.who: Any person holding the uncancelled identity card of a deceased person.
steps.trigger: Coming into possession of the card.

deadline.text: within 30 days of coming into possession

steps.summary: The card must be handed in or posted to the Director-General within 30 days for cancellation and destruction (a relative may ask to keep it).

steps.title: State departments obtain death data from the register
steps.who: The Director-General, to any State department, municipality or statutory body.
steps.trigger: A department's request for its statutory purposes.
steps.summary: Population-register and death-notice information may be furnished to State departments for their statutory purposes; the specific feeds to SASSA, SARS, GEPF or the IEC are not in these Acts.

steps.title: Banks and insurers may be given population-register data
steps.who: Banks (Banks Act 1990) and insurers, and other bodies, subject to prescribed conditions and fees.
steps.summary: The Identification Act expressly allows the Director-General to furnish population-register information, including death particulars, to banks and insurers on prescribed terms. The operational online verification service was not sourced.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: No fixed period: notice must be given 'as soon as practicable' (1992 text as enacted; later amendments and the 2014 regulations not read).

informantDuty.note: Any person present at the death, who became aware of it, or who has charge of the burial.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent review; unnatural deaths go to the police and the magistrate under the Inquests Act.

electronicRegistration.note: Not established from the Act; Home Affairs' electronic notification practice not sourced.

centralPopulationRegister.name: National Population Register
centralPopulationRegister.note: National Population Register under the Identification Act; inclusion in it is the registration of the death.

governmentPropagation.note: Registration is entry in the population register itself, which departments may read for statutory purposes; the specific feeds to SASSA, SARS and the IEC were not sourced.

certificateAccess.note: Death certificates are issued on application; the Acts do not say who may apply. Information is otherwise secret except as s. 29 allows.

privateSectorVerification.note: Statutory route: the Director-General may furnish population-register information to banks, insurers and other bodies on prescribed terms (Identification Act s. 21(2)).

gaps: The Births and Deaths Registration Act text read is the 1992 Government Gazette as enacted (gov.za OCR PDF). Amendments (incl. Act 18 of 2010) and the Regulations on the Registration of Births and Deaths 2014 were not read; any fixed notice period (e.g. 72 hours in the regulations) is unverified. saflii.org (consolidated text) and lawlibrary.org.za were blocked by the egress proxy (CONNECT 403).

Home Affairs' online death-verification service for banks (via the NPR/HANIS) was not found in an official source reachable from here; dha.gov.za was not reached. Only the statutory basis (Identification Act s. 21(2)) is cited.

Feeds from the NPR to SASSA (social grants), SARS, GEPF and the IEC voters' roll were not sourced; the Electoral Act 73 of 1998 (s. 11) allows deregistration of voters who no longer qualify but does not mention deaths or the NPR.
Who may apply for a death certificate is set by regulation, not read.
The 1992 PDF has OCR noise; quotes keep its spelling (e.g. 'presctibed', 'anv').
